newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power dips amid easing transmission.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power dips amid easing transmission.

text.p: Physical wholesale electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. fell Friday ahead of the U.S. Columbus Day holiday weekend amid cool autumn weather and easing transmission limitations, market sources said.

The expected return of Georgia Power Co's 1,162 megawatt (MW) Vogtle 2 nuclear power plant in Waynesboro, Ga., this weekend from its refueling outage was expected to ease the loop flow problem at the Southern Co's interface at the Georgia/Florida border, traders said.
"That should help the power system. They have loop flow problem from North to South. The return of Vogtle should provide power to northern Georgia," said a Houston trader.
Transmission contraint at Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) southern network with Southern Co were heard lifted today. There was a reported 200-600 MW transmission cut at that point Thursday.
Next-day electricity for firm, peak delivery into the northern area of TVA was quoted for Saturday at $14.00-$15.00 a megawatt hour (MWh); Sunday $13.00-$14.00; and Monday $15.00-$16.00.
On Thursday, next-day power prices into northern TVA were assessed at $15.00-$17.00.
Down at the Ga./Fla. border, firm, peak electricity was valued for Saturday at $21.25-$21.75; Sunday $21.00-$21.50; and Monday $22.25-$22.50.
Thursday's power values at the Ga./Fla. border for Friday delivery was pegged at $22.00-$23.00 a MWh.
TVA was reportedly offering peak, non-firm electricity for Saturday at $16.75; Sunday $16.50; and Monday $19.00, compared with Thursday's $17.50 for Friday.
Southern Nuclear Operation Co will shut the 822 MW Farley 2 nuclear power unit in Dothan, Ala., on Saturday for scheduled refueling and maintenance. The outage was planned for at least a month.
